U3: Add refuse-mode admission to the codex fleet-core lease broker. Read docs/plans/2026-07-25-codex-refreeze-627-seam-and-cor3-worktree-authority-plan.md as your authoritative spec; U3, requirement R5, and KTD3/KTD5/KTD6 govern this unit.

FIRST TASK, BEFORE ANY EDIT -- resolve KTD6. Codex carries TWO lease_broker.py files: plugins/saga/scripts/lease_broker.py (542 lines) and plugins/fleet-core/scripts/fleet_commons/lease_broker.py (4183 lines). Only the fleet-core copy carries _drop_superseded_resource_lease (2 refs) and _owner_state (3 refs); the saga copy carries neither. Determine what the saga copy IS -- vendored shim, stale duplicate, or deliberate narrow subset -- and state the finding explicitly. R5 targets the fleet-core copy. If the saga copy also needs the mode, that is a scope change to SURFACE, not to absorb silently.

Then implement requirement R5 EXACTLY as the plan quotes it. READ THE REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION -- Claude plugins/fleet-core/scripts/fleet_commons/lease_broker.py:2375-2425 -- and do NOT work from the issue comment's one-line summary, which is an incomplete paraphrase.

The signature gains `on_conflict: OnConflict = "supersede"`. The refusal is a THREE-PART conjunction: `prior_lease is not None` AND `not self._expired(prior_lease, monotonic=monotonic, boot_id=boot_id)` AND `self._owner_state(prior_lease) != "dead"`. Each arm has its own fall-through-to-supersede case -- a MISSING prior_lease supersedes; an EXPIRED prior is reclaimed in BOTH modes because the TTL+boot-id check precedes the liveness probe; a provably DEAD owner supersedes with no TTL wait. Only live and unknown on an UNEXPIRED prior refuse. A one-part reading that checks only _owner_state is wrong and will silently drop the expired-reclaim arm.

R5a: the refusal raises LeaseConflictError carrying holder_owner_id=prior_lease.owner_id -- not a bare exception, not LeaseOwnershipError.

R5b: refuse-mode is gated BELOW two existing precedence checks that must keep firing first and must not be reordered -- retained settlement authority and canonically-closed-requires-acquire_successor, both LeaseOwnershipError.

Default-mode call sites must be byte-identical in behavior. Claude's copy carries on_conflict x9, _owner_state x5, "refuse" x6; codex's carries 0, 3, 0.

PORT THE FULL PUBLIC CONTRACT, NOT ONLY THE PRIVATE BRANCH. codex has ZERO occurrences of both OnConflict and LeaseConflictError, so adding only the private _drop_superseded_resource_lease branch leaves LeaseBroker.acquire_agent(on_conflict="refuse") unsupported -- U4 would get TypeError and _lease_conflict_error_type() would have no typed conflict to recognize. Enumerate and port ALL of: the OnConflict = Literal["supersede", "refuse"] alias (Claude :46), class LeaseConflictError(LeaseOwnershipError) with its holder_owner_id metadata (Claude :241), the public acquire_agent on_conflict parameter and default (Claude :2486+), its closed-value validation, the passthrough to the private helper, and subclass compatibility. Verify each against Claude b464d090 before porting.

Extend plugins/fleet-core/tests/test_lease_broker.py with ALL ELEVEN scenarios U3 lists -- one per arm of the conjunction, plus both precedence gates, plus the two fall-through cases. The live-owner refusal must assert the prior lease's registry bytes are byte-for-byte untouched AND that holder_owner_id is populated, not merely that a refusal was returned. The expired-prior-is-reclaimed scenario is the one most likely to be missed.

KTD5 is absolute: if you find a defect in the shared upstream mechanism, STOP and report it for upstream filing against infiquetra-claude-plugins. Never fix it codex-side.

units.label: dispatcher transient-error arm and reconcile re-raise ordering
units.worth_it_because: the deliverable is an ORDERING guarantee -- a non-transient DispatcherError must abort the tick BEFORE lease release and ledger writes -- and an implementation that releases first still raises, so it passes any test that only asserts the exception type; proving the guarantee needs a test that inspects lease and ledger state at the moment of the raise, plus a shim-load-failure path that must decline to transient rather than assume it, and the reconcile hot path lives in outcome.py in codex rather than outcome_reconcile.py as in Claude.

Add DispatcherLeaseTransientError(DispatcherError) raised at lease-conflict admission sites, classified through a shim-safe _lease_conflict_error_type() that DECLINES to transient when the shim fails to load. Make _reconcile_once re-raise any NON-transient DispatcherError BEFORE lease release and ledger writes, so permanent faults abort the tick loudly; only the transient subclass keeps halt-and-continue.

Preserve codex's own outcome.dispatch.v2 intent and acknowledgement contract -- that string lives in plugins/saga/references/outcome-cross-runtime.md, plugins/saga/references/run-fact-ledger.md, and plugins/saga/tests/test_outcome_board_sync.py. The load-bearing test is the ordering one, and requirement R7a is precise about WHICH lock: at the moment of the non-transient re-raise the per-subplot `dispatch-{sid}` STORE lock is STILL HELD (deliberate; self-heals after the 900 s DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL), the 300 s BROKER dispatch lease is ALREADY RELEASED by make_dispatcher's own finally before this arm runs, and the coordinator lock is released by the outer finally.
